title: Registry of Responsibility
subtitle: Not an abstract 'system' but identifiable individuals whose decisions formed a chain of arbitrariness.
intro: The prosecution of Dmitry Lagovsky is not an error or a random malfunction. It is a documented sequence of actions by specific officials. Some converted a commercial dispute into a criminal narrative, others provided judicial cover, and others legitimised violations through formalistic oversight refusals. This registry records each individual's role in the destruction of justice.

items.label: Initiators
items.title: Corporate Motive and Criminalisation
items.desc: Individuals who moved a lost arbitration dispute into the criminal sphere. Sergei Palkin's group used law enforcement mechanisms as leverage in a private conflict.

items.label: Executors
items.title: The Investigative Apparatus
items.desc: The investigative group (Salikov, Chugunkov, Kuznetsov) who ensured the fabrication of evidence, secret indictment, and unlawful international wanted notice.

items.label: Legitimisers
items.title: Prosecutorial Oversight and Collusion
items.desc: Prosecution officials (Mitrokhina, Prokopenko) who transformed oversight into a technical relay of the investigator's version through template refusals.

items.label: Judicial Barrier
items.title: Elimination of Access to Justice
items.desc: Judges (Semina, Krivoruchko, Gasnikova) who provided judicial sanction for the arbitrariness and blocked Lagovsky's right to defense under Article 125 CCP.

items.name: Sergei Valentinovich Palkin
items.role: Vice-President of OZHPT, Director at LLC TC EurazHolding. Complainant.
items.action: Initiated criminal prosecution after a series of defeats in arbitration courts. His actions are a classic example of weaponising criminal justice to settle scores in a corporate dispute.

items.name: Yuriy Mikhaylovich Salikov
items.role: Investigator at Moscow Region Main Investigation Department (retired).
items.doc: Decision opening the case; search protocols.
items.action: The primary procedural executor of the initial stage. Opened the case despite the lack of a 'victim's' complaint, conducted searches against a court order, and built a foundation of 'distorted' evidence.

items.name: I.I. Chugunkov
items.role: Deputy Head of 6th Section at Moscow Region GSU.
items.action: Took over the mantle of arbitrariness from Salikov. Signs identical template responses, completely ignoring facts about res judicata and proof of fabrication provided by the defense.

items.name: E.I. Kuznetsov
items.role: Head of 6th Section at Moscow Region GSU. Investigative team leader.
items.action: Ensures departmental 'impenetrability'. Personally reviews complaints against his own subordinates, invariably confirming the legality of their actions — a structural paralysis of internal control.

items.name: A.A. Mitrokhina
items.role: Deputy Head of Department at Moscow Region Prosecutor's Office.
items.action: The face of prosecutorial blindness. Over a year, she issued a series of identical brush-offs ('no violations found'), de-facto delegating oversight to the investigators themselves.

items.name: S.V. Prokopenko
items.action: Finalised the refusal system at the federal level. In his responses, Lagovsky's presumption of innocence is substituted with references to the convictions of third parties.

items.name: Olga Nikolaevna Semina
items.role: Judge at the Tverskoy District Court of Moscow.
items.doc: Rulings on the return of complaints (2026).
items.action: Ensures the 'judicial blockade'. Returns defense complaints without consideration on formal pretexts, stripping the accused of the only lawful way to challenge investigative abuse.

items.name: Aleksey Vyacheslavovich Krivoruchko
items.role: Judge at the Tverskoy District Court of Moscow (Magnitsky List).
items.action: Issued the ruling on arrest in absentia and wanted status despite the defendant's known location, thereby creating the formal basis for the extradition request.

summary: This registry proves that we are dealing not with an abstract legal collision, but with a managed process. Every refusal, every signature, and every unlawful decision has an author who bears personal responsibility for violating international human rights standards.
